claims.statement: The production catalog recognizes ring, earrings, necklace, pendant, bracelet and brooch/pin as jewelry item types used by the current product model.
claims.scope: Jewelry item type taxonomy for Product State v1

claims.statement: GIA's Gem Encyclopedia presents alexandrite, amber, amethyst, ametrine, aquamarine, citrine, diamond, emerald, garnet, iolite, jade, kunzite, lapis lazuli, moonstone, morganite, opal, pearl, peridot, rose quartz, ruby, sapphire, spinel, sunstone, tanzanite, topaz, tourmaline, turquoise and zircon as named gem materials or gem entries.

Gem shape describes outline while cut style describes facet arrangement; round, oval, pear, marquise, cushion, heart, square, rectangular, octagonal and triangular outlines must remain distinct from brilliant, step and other cutting styles.
Brilliant, step, mixed and rose are distinct faceting styles, while cabochon is a non-faceted fashioning style; outline shape is a separate attribute.
Prong, bezel, flush, channel, tension, bar, basket and pavé are recognized gemstone-setting methods or setting structures; setting method is distinct from overall ring design style.
Solitaire, three-stone, cathedral, halo and toi et moi are ring design or setting styles and must remain distinct from the mechanical method that secures a gemstone.
CIBJO precious-metal nomenclature includes platinum, gold, palladium and silver, and defines fineness as precious-metal content expressed in parts per thousand by weight of alloy.
Jewelry gold is commonly described in yellow, white and rose color variants; color is a separate design attribute from the metal material itself.
JewelAI Contract v1 requires rose gold and red gold to remain distinct canonical metal-color concepts.
A ring mounting includes a shank and head; shoulders connect the shank toward the head, and basket structures can support and stabilize gemstone settings.

The production catalog uses the GIA Gem Encyclopedia's broad color vocabulary including colorless, white, yellow, pink, red, blue, green, purple, orange, brown, black and gray as non-grading color descriptors.
claims.scope: General gemstone color descriptors; not laboratory grading scales

claims.statement: JewelAI Production Catalog v1 defines bounded canonical product vocabulary for metal finish, stone orientation, selected construction terms and general aesthetic styles where the current Product State has fields but external quantitative facts are not required.

Carat weight is mass and does not determine physical dimensions; center-stone role does not imply material; qualitative shank width has no universal millimetre thresholds; white gold does not imply rhodium coating.

policies.effect: Normalize only explicit or accepted jewelry type; do not infer type from occasion or style.
Do not infer metal material from color, finish or visual appearance.
Preserve rose/red distinction; color does not imply coating and white gold does not imply rhodium.
Preserve explicit purity value and unit; do not derive purity from material, color or appearance.
Use only explicit or accepted finish vocabulary; do not infer finish from metal material.
Center-stone role does not imply diamond or any material.
Shape is independent from cut style; normalize only explicit or context-resolved shape.
Cut style is independent from outline shape; do not infer brilliant or step cut from shape alone.
Carat weight is mass; do not infer dimensions from weight in the semantic catalog.
Dimensions require explicit or separately sourced quantitative evidence; do not infer from carat weight.
Use explicit or accepted stone-color information; do not infer color from material.
Setting type is separate from prong count and overall design style.
Use explicit or accepted orientation only.
Use explicit construction information; do not invent shank geometry.
Use explicit construction information; do not infer gallery geometry from setting style.
Use explicit construction information; do not infer basket geometry from stone shape.
Use explicit clasp information only.
Setting height requires explicit or separately sourced dimensional evidence.
Do not translate qualitative width into universal millimetre thresholds.
Thickness requires explicit or separately sourced dimensional evidence.
Style is separate from occasion and from the mechanical stone-setting method.
Bind only an existing stable side-stone group; do not infer material from center stone.
Bind only an existing stable side-stone group; shape is independent from cut style.
Bind only an existing stable side-stone group; do not infer cut from shape.
Bind only an existing stable side-stone group; do not infer dimensions from weight.
Bind only an existing stable side-stone group; dimensions require explicit or sourced quantitative evidence.
Bind only an existing stable side-stone group; do not infer color from material.
Bind only an existing stable side-stone group; setting type is independent from prong count.
Bind only an existing stable side-stone group; use explicit or accepted orientation only.
Bind quantity only to an existing stable side-stone group and preserve explicit scope.
